claims.statement: The concept declares FPT/GHEC/GHES; its category and title are contextual metadata, not accepted policy.
Workflow, custom-action and composite-action authors should always consider whether attacker-controlled context strings can be interpreted as code on the runner.

The source recommends treating potentially attacker-controlled context fields with suffixes body, default_branch, email, head_ref, label, message, name, page_name, ref and title as untrusted input rather than trusted program text.

The source recommends ensuring untrusted values do not flow directly into workflows, actions, APIs or other execution positions where they can become code. This is partial injection-boundary support, not an adopted local prohibition or a completed detector.
Branch names and email addresses are less obvious untrusted inputs; permitted syntax can contain shell-significant content. Valid metadata syntax is not shell safety.

The inline PR-title example is vulnerable because expressions are evaluated and substituted into a temporary shell script before execution; surrounding quotes do not make arbitrary substituted text safe.

The screenshot and output demonstrate a title interrupting assignment quoting and introducing a listing command. This is an illustrative attack, not an instruction to execute it or proof of current target exploitability.
The mitigation-practices link points outside this article; no linked artifact or effective remediation is credited from the reference alone.
